short: The first complete tank prototype, built in Lincoln and never sent to war.
full:
Built by William Foster and Co. of Lincoln for the Admiralty's Landships Committee, the No. 1 Lincoln Machine first ran in September 1915. It was a riveted steel box on tracks bought from the Bullock Creeping Grip Tractor Company of Chicago, powered by a 105 hp Daimler engine, with a wheeled tail for steering. A turret was designed for it but never fitted; ballast was carried instead.

The machine shed its tracks constantly, so it was rebuilt with longer track frames of Foster design and retested in December 1915, by which time it had acquired the name Little Willie. Even improved, it could not meet the War Office requirement to cross an eight-foot trench and climb a four-and-a-half-foot parapet. That demand produced the rhomboid hull of the machine called Mother, which became the Mark I. Little Willie never entered service; the original vehicle survives at the Tank Museum, Bovington.
